voyage.name: Museum of the Revolution
voyage.content: Housed in the former presidential palace, this iconic museum offers a history tour from pre-Columbian to the revolution in 1959 and on to present-day socialist Cuba. There's more than a hint of propaganda among the exhibitions.

voyage.name: National Capitol Building
voyage.content: Completed in 1929, this neoclassical building which resembles the U.S. Capitol. It housed the Cuban Congress prior to the revolution and is now the National Assembly.

voyage.name: Partagás Cigar factory
voyage.price: the equivalent of US$10 in pesos for a guided tour, no photography allowed
voyage.content: A guided visit to the original Partagás factory gives a wealth of information about production and cultivation of tobacco and cigars. It is also the place for buying authentic Cuban cigars, more expensive than on the street but with fantastic quality.

voyage.name: Havana Club Rum Museum
voyage.content: Go on a guided tour of Havana Club, one of Cuba's most famous rums. Most of the exhibits are subtitled in English and are fairly self-explanatory.

voyage.name: Plaza de la Revolución
voyage.content: Huge square dominated by a statue and monument of Jose Marti and the iconic image of Che Guevara adorning the Ministry of the Interior. Arrive either early or late, as it is often swamped by tourists and gets very hot during the day.

voyage.name: Lennon Park
voyage.content: Features the only statue of a western musician in Havana. Notable for the regularly stolen (and replaced) eyeglasses.

voyage.name: US Embassy
voyage.content: This heavily fortified and guarded building is where Cuban citizens go to apply for U.S. visas. It was notable for displaying news which was unfiltered and not censored by the Cuban government on electronic billboards behind the windows of one of the floors, but these were switched off in 2009. It is also the focus for regularly staged protests.

voyage.name: Hotel Habana Libre
voyage.content: The hotel housed Castro's soldiers for several days after they took Havana. It has an excellent selection of photos in the lobby along with one of the only 24-hr fast food restaurants in the city.

voyage.name: Fabrica de Arte Cubano
voyage.alt: La Fábrica de Arte or FAC
voyage.content: An art gallery and club. The Fábrica's gallery and stage were established inside of a former cooking oil factory, and has since gained notoriety as one of Havana's premier nightclubs and art galas.

voyage.name: Cámara Oscura
voyage.content: Enjoy extraordinary 360° views of the city using the large Cámara Oscura in the old town.

voyage.name: Havana Cathedral
voyage.content: Built in the 18th century and redesigned in the 1940s, this church is a prime example of Baroque architecture in Cuba. Houses the seat of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese in Cuba.

voyage.name: Plaza de Armas
voyage.content: Spacious and elegant, the square is surrounded by baroque constructions that give it an authentic colonial milieu. It was laid out during the 1600s, replacing an old plaza which acted as the center of religious, administrative and military activity. Until the mid-18th century, it was used for military exercises and parades. After its remodeling between the years 1771-1838, it became a favored meeting spot for the cit

voyage.name: The Royal Force Castle
voyage.content: The oldest bastioned fortress in the New World, completed 1577. It now houses Cuba's premier maritime museum with excellent exhibits of Cuba’s maritime past, from pre-Columbian days through to the 18th century with the Royal Shipyard of Havana, one of the largest in the world which built nearly 200 ships for the Spanish Crown. The museum includes a huge model of Santisima Trinidad, one of the largest ships in the wor

voyage.name: Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes
voyage.address: Trocadero, btwn Agraminte and Av de las Misiones
voyage.content: This museum has two parts: international and Cuban art. In the part of Arte Cubano art-lovers can spend hours admiring the works of the last centuries exhibited on three floors.

voyage.name: Fortaleza de San Carlos de la Cabaña
voyage.content: A well-restored fort of the 18th century that holds two one-room exhibitions about arms and Che Guevara. Every evening there is a cannon ceremony where they fire over the Havana harbour. To get there take any bus (ex. from the Parque the la Fraternidad) that crosses the tunnel and get off right after it. Walk about 600 m to the entrance. On your way you can also stop at the smaller Castillo de los Tres Santos Reyes M

voyage.name: Colon Cemetery
voyage.content: One of the great historical cemeteries of the world, important in both historical and architectural terms. It's not possible to see much from behind the fence.

voyage.name: Walk along the Malecón
voyage.content: On weekends this is where the locals come to party, so bring a bottle and join in.

voyage.name: Walk down the Paseo del Prado
voyage.content: A lively pedestrian zone full of locals spending their free time.

voyage.name: Latin American New Cinema Festival
voyage.content: A popular event held every December, screening international films and drawing around 500,000 people.

voyage.name: Bike tour, Discover Havana by bike
voyage.address: 117 San Francisco street, Centro Habana, between San Lázaro St. and Jovellar St. Havana
voyage.content: Citykleta offers you a wide range of shared or private bike tours, bike excursions and events in Havana through which you can get to know the city like no other.

voyage.name: Take a tour in an old car
voyage.content: Be driven around Havana in style. Choose a car you like near the Hotel Inglaterra or outside the Museum of the Revolution.

voyage.name: Go to the eastern beaches
voyage.content: There is a bus leaving from Hotel Inglaterra every 30 minutes. The ride takes about 30 minutes.

voyage.name: National Theater
voyage.content: Come here for concerts, the Ballet Nacional de Cuba and teatre. Functions are held irregularly. Beware of scams as ushers try to sell you the same ticket for up to ~US$25 shortly before the function starts (and only paying the nationals price). Instead go to the box office to get it for the official price.

voyage.name: Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes
voyage.content: Regularly has live music events that often cost only 250 CUP. Check their Facebook page for the announcements

voyage.name: Hotel National
voyage.content: Often hosts big name talent such as Omara Portuondo. See also information below.

voyage.name: La Zorra y el Cuervo, La Rampa
voyage.content: A tiny little club below street level, they often host funky and amazing jazz musicians. Go there for something a little different.

voyage.name: La Tropical
voyage.content: A venue designed to hold several thousand people. It only opens for live music. Look around for signs in the streets publicising the next event.

voyage.name: Casa de la Musica de Centro Habana
voyage.content: The place to be if you like to dance Salsa. Check the program before you buy tickets, there are different top-rated Salsa bands playing every night.

voyage.name: Museo del Ron
voyage.content: Offers a very nice outdoors 1950s Cuban music show called Buena Vista. You can watch it with or without dinner.

voyage.name: Bertolt Brecht Cultural Center
voyage.address: 258, 13th street, Vedado. Between I street and J street
voyage.content: Go dance with Interactivo on Wednesday nights. Interactivo is a collaborative group of Cuban musicians, led by the pianist, singer and composer Roberto Carcasses.

voyage.name: Tropicana Show
voyage.content: A cabaret 1950s show, a must-see show while you are in Havana.

voyage.name: Legendarios del Guajirito
voyage.content: Similar to the Tropicana show but smaller and more immersive. Once the live show ends, the venue turns into a nightclub till around 02:00.

voyage.name: Coppelia Ice Cream parlour
voyage.content: Practically a Cuban institution with people waiting up to an hour to get a seat.

voyage.name: Chan Li Po
voyage.content: The restaurant is upstairs, fully air-conditioned, looks immaculate. Despite being a Chinese restaurant, they serve European dishes too. Friendly service. About ~US$4 for one pizza. Cocktails are ~US$2.5.

voyage.name: Hanoi
voyage.address: Corner of Teniente Rey and Bernaza
voyage.content: Old fashioned restaurant, with live music and no A/C. They even serve traditional Cuban food, such as black beans with rice.

voyage.name: El Aljibe
voyage.content: In the Havana suburb of Miramar, El Aljibe is the definitive proof that food in Cuba needn't be bland. Try the house specialty, chicken in sour orange sauce. El Aljibe also has a remarkably well-stocked wine cellar.

voyage.name: La Casa
voyage.content: This stylish restaurant, in Nuevo Vedado, is a large California-style house typical of the 1950s. The dining room and garden are inviting and intimate. The impeccable service and consistency uncommon in Cuba, are a must in Havana.

voyage.name: Paladar La Tasquita
voyage.address: Calle 27 de Noviembre (Jovellar No. 160) e/ Espada y San Francisco
voyage.content: Located near San Lazaro, this Paladar (small, family-run, privately-owned restaurant) serves typical criolla food. You will be dining in the living room of a local family, so don't expect anything glamorous in terms of atmosphere. On the other hand, the staff is very friendly and you will get the opportunity to taste typical Cuban food as local families prepare it: Simply delicious. The seating is limited so reserve

voyage.name: DNext Bar Cafetería
voyage.content: They serve mainly Italian food, sandwiches and cocktails. Prices start at ~US$3.5. The establishment is fully air-conditioned and ideal for a quick meal.

voyage.name: Los Marinos
voyage.content: Seafood restaurant on a pier in Havana harbour. A great place to relax with seafood and a beer or mojito looking at the city. On the big terrace the breeze from the water is pleasant on a warm day. Prices depends on the kind of seafood, you order. Lobster is the most expensive. The seafood paella is less expensive, has lots of good seafood in it, and you get a big portion.

voyage.name: Castropol
voyage.content: Restaurant with Cuban-Asturian food. Lots of great appetizers that also works as snacks with a cocktail. The atmosphere is cosy. In front of the restaurant is a small arcade with small cast iron tables and chairs, where you can have a drink (and a snack) and look over the water and study the steady stream of old US cars on Malecon (you just have to accept the noise from the cars too).

voyage.name: La Fontana Restaurant
voyage.content: One of the most notable grill restaurants in Cuba. La Fontana has a refined yet sober home environment, suitable for a dinner with a touch of familiarity and a placid conversation, while enjoying exquisite dishes from its specialty, updated Cuban cuisine. Reservations essential.

voyage.name: La Bodeguita del Medio
voyage.content: The bar in which to sample a Mojito. The former hangout of Ernest Hemingway, it is best sampled in the evening once the tourist crowds from Varadero have headed back out of the city.

voyage.name: El Floridita Bar
voyage.content: Another stop on the Hemingway drinking tour; best visited for its atmosphere, which is almost unchanged from pre-Castro days. Their daiquirís are however - certainly much to Hemingway's grievance - mediocre.

voyage.name: Los Buccaneros Hanoi
voyage.content: With the front of the Capitol building on your right from the main street, walk about two blocks to the left on the road that runs parallel to the Capitol. There are two bars called Hanoi. Go to the first one Los Buccaneros.

voyage.name: Factoría Plaza Vieja
voyage.price: ~US$2 for a glass of beer, ~US$12.50 for a 'meter' of beer.
voyage.content: Brewpub located on the pretty Plaza Vieja. The pub has three main beers (light, dark and black), with seasonal additions. Beer cocktails, along with a meat-based food menu, also feature.

voyage.name: Casa Ana & Surama
voyage.price: €25-60 Depending room and how may persons and when
voyage.address: San Ignacio no 454 2º piso entre Sol y Vieja Santa Clara La Habana Cuba
voyage.content: Clean house in colonial style, like you are time travelling, see the pictures on website of our casa.

voyage.name: Casa "Todo de Aitana"
voyage.address: 14 street, #51, between Linea Ave. and 11 street, Vedado
voyage.content: Full apartment for 1-3 guest. The apartment is very nice, quiet and clean, with views to the sea and sunsets. 1 bedroom, bathroom, kitchen, nice balcony. You can reserve on Airbnb https://www.airbnb.com/rooms/15798248/

voyage.name: Ana y Chuchi
voyage.content: Very central place with a great host who gets out of her way to make people comfortable. Three rooms of different sizes. Small windows overlook patio, breakfast and dinner are enormous.

voyage.name: Casa Mabel
voyage.address: Industria No. 270 (altos), between Neptuno and Virtudes, Centro Habana
voyage.content: A very friendly family home. 2 comfortable rooms with balcony and great view for rent.

voyage.name: Jorge Leon de la Hoz
voyage.address: Neptuno No. 1218 (altos), e/ Mazon y Basarrate, Vedado Plaza
voyage.content: A very friendly family home, close to the Universidad de la Habana. Room rates are negotiable depending upon the length of stay.

voyage.name: Señores Elsa y Julio Roque
voyage.address: Consulado No. 162, apto. 2 (between Colon and Trocadero)
voyage.content: A very friendly couple rent rooms in their centrally located house, and help find other houses in case they're full. Both speak good English and offer helpful information. Reservations can be made by e-mail either in English or in Spanish

voyage.name: Casa Olga
voyage.content: Olga rents her entire 2nd floor including full kitchen, living room and three beds (one double) for ~US$25-30. She's extremely friendly and not pushy like other casa owners can be.

voyage.name: Señora Ivette Flores
voyage.content: Rents out three private rooms with air conditioning and independent entrances

voyage.name: Casa Mra Cristina & Guillermo
voyage.address: Calle 21 e/N and O - Building #15 Apartment 7-A, Vedado
voyage.content: A very friendly family home with two university-aged children who speak English. 2 comfortable rooms with balcony and great view. Ask for "mi cafecita" in the morning on the balcony.

voyage.name: Casa de Jesus y Saida Valdez,Calle 24 #262, Apt #5
Casa de Lydia y Felix Pedro
La Casa de Ana
voyage.address: 17 St #1422, Apt 1 (between 26 st and 28 st), Vedado

voyage.name: Alicia Beaton, Havana
voyage.address: CRESPO No. 10, e/ San Lazaro y Malecon, Vedado
voyage.content: This is very convenient hostel, located close to the Malecon and near the Park Central area. The pristine house and bedrooms are located on the third floor of the building. Ask the owners to turn off the air conditioning if you are too cold.

voyage.name: Casa Nora, Havana
voyage.content: Living room, bedroom and compact kitchen. George speaks wonderful English and has a wealth of information.

voyage.name: Casa Nora, Havana
voyage.address: Calle 27 No. 954 e/ 6 y 8 apt 4, Vedado, Habana
voyage.content: Casa Nora is a lovely apartment right in the heart of Vedado. Her wonderful, friendly family makes you feel at right at home. Very safe area. The rooms are very big with AC and television, and they have an incredible view of Vedado and the ocean. Great food as well.

voyage.name: Sra. Ivón de los Angeles Acosta
voyage.address: Central no. 2 entre Conil y Tulipán, Nuevo Vedado, Plaza de la Revolucion
voyage.content: Nice roof terrace just for you, great meals and super friendly hosts.

voyage.name: Casa Tere
voyage.price: ~US$25/night, 1 room with air con, 2 single bed
voyage.address: Consulado no. 303, entre Neptuno y Virtudes, Havana Center

voyage.name: Casa 1932
voyage.price: ~US$30/night, 2 room with air con, 2 single bed & one double bed
voyage.address: Campanario 63 bajos entre San Lazaro y Lagunas, Havana Center

voyage.name: Casa Milagros Diez
voyage.price: from ~US$25/night, 2 double rooms with en suite bathroom accessible for people in wheelchairs

voyage.name: Casa Xiomara Hernández
voyage.content: Calle Aguila No. 506 Derecha 2do. Piso -right entrance of the building, second floor; entre San Jose y Barcelona.

voyage.name: Casa Lázaro
voyage.address: Villegas #427 between Teniente Rey and Muralla
voyage.content: Old construction, very well preserved. Offers breakfast, dinner, taxi, and laundry services among others.

voyage.name: Hostel Carpizon
voyage.content: The hostel is composed by two houses each one located on very centrical places. Also you can enjoy of very comfortable rooms which include terrace and backyards.

voyage.name: Sizemore Habana
voyage.address: Calle Habana No 923 Altos, Habana Vieja
voyage.content: Very lovely place with an amazing host (Belkis) who is very generous and helpful. Two rooms with two double beds and private bathrooms.

voyage.name: Ricardo's Place
voyage.content: Private apartment with terrace (for guests only). Free breakfast. Kitchen. Air conditioning. Good water pressure. And Internet (extra fee, optional). Not a touristic area so the plus is “this is the real Cuba”. 20 minutes away from the center (Old Havana aka Habana Vieja). A bank, cafeterias, bars, mini markets, all at no more than 3 blocks away (literally). An indoor garage is also available at no extra charge.

voyage.name: Casa Vitrales
voyage.content: Upmarket, stylish casa particular in Old Havana with choice of room category and roof terrace.

voyage.name: Near Airport
voyage.content: There are several places to stay located 15 minutes of walking distance away from the airport, which is practical for very early flights

voyage.name: Hamel Hostel
voyage.content: 12-bed dorm.

voyage.name: D Robles Hostel
voyage.content: four-bed dorms

voyage.name: Enzo's Backpackers Hostel
voyage.content: A dorm with six beds

voyage.name: Hotel Inglaterra
voyage.content: Paseo del Prado, Old Havana. A popular hotel with a restaurant for those wanting to stay closer to the action yet still in the comforts of a hotel.

voyage.name: Hotel Mercure Sevilla Havane
voyage.address: Trocadero 55 e, Prado y Zulueta Habana Vieja

voyage.name: Hotel Telegrafo
voyage.price: US$80–120, cheaper if you book ahead with Opodo
voyage.content: A popular hotel just around the corner from Parque Central, right next to Inglaterra. Renovated and now really nice inside, a welcome haven of peace away from Vieja.

voyage.name: Tryp Habana Libre Hotel
voyage.content: A Havana landmark in a good location, it's popular with tourists and journalists, has a good 24-hr cafe on site, and a business center with decent internet connections.

voyage.name: Hotel Habana Riviera
voyage.content: Paseo and Malecón, Vedado. Located along the Malecon, Havana's waterfront boulevard, this elegant hotel is considered a classic among Cubans. Its proximity to the historical-cultural center of Havana, makes this hotel the perfect place from which to explore the city. In the night time the Riviera offers excellent entertainment featuring both the exclusive Copa Room Cabaret and one of Havana's top restaurants.

voyage.name: Hotel Nacional de Cuba
voyage.content: Calle 21 and O, Vedado. Overlooking the ocean on the Malecón, this hotel is legendary, having hosted international VIPs for 30 years. Many years of neglect, coupled with an only partially successful renovation, have left the Nacional a step below its former glory. That said, some stay here and rarely leave the hotel, enjoying the restaurant, terrace, frequent live performances by renowned Cuban musicians, and enjoyin

voyage.name: Hotel Parque Central
voyage.content: Similar to the Saratoga in quality, and has a beautiful ground floor lobby and a rooftop swimming pool. The Torre wing may have the best rooms in Cuba, at least by Western standards. The lobby of the Torre is very good, in keeping with the main hotel lobby. Excellent breakfast buffet.

voyage.name: Hotel Conde de Villanueva
voyage.address: Calle Mercaderes esq. Amagura, Old Havana
voyage.content: A beautifully restored colonial home, this hotel is the ultimate destination for a connoisseur of Cuban cigars; each room is named after a tobacco plantation, and, of course, all rooms permit smoking. Boasts an impressive cigar shop in the hotel, in addition to a (reasonably average) restaurant. Be warned, though: if you like to sleep late, there is a peacock that wanders around the courtyard that begins to make nois

voyage.name: Hotel Ambos Mundos
voyage.content: Writer Ernest Hemingway stayed and wrote most of For Whom the Bell Tolls here, a fact which adds historical charm to this well-located hotel in Old Havana. The Plaza de Armas is a few steps away, and the establishment has an elegant and lively lobby where piano and jazz musicians perform.

voyage.name: Hotel Park View
voyage.content: Colón 101. A popular hotel in the 1920s, the Park View is a small establishment just off Prado, close to the colonial centre of Old Havana and the seawall. It does not share in the historical or decorative charm of other Old Havana properties, but it is certainly a practical option for anyone interested in exploring Old Havana and traveling on a tighter budget.

voyage.name: Hotel Plaza
voyage.content: The Plaza is one of Havana’s oldest hotels. In addition to a beautifully restored interior and a great location near many places of interest in Old Havana, the hotel also has some interesting anecdotes. Albert Einstein once dined here, and Babe Ruth stayed at one of the suites, today a museum (where his bat has been preserved).

voyage.name: Hotel Santa Isabel
voyage.content: Considered Old Havana’s flagship hotel, this establishment is one of the classier – and more expensive – colonial-era options in this part of town. The long terrace overlooking the Plaza de Armas, shared by 10 west-facing rooms, is one of the hotel’s most evident charms, as are its colonial appeal and a magnificent location.

voyage.name: Hotel Meliá La Habana
voyage.content: A modern five-star hotel with very big and comfortable rooms, and possibly the biggest swimming pool in Havana.
